subjects.title: Immunology

subjects.title: Microbiology & Antimicrobials
subjects.description: The existing sterilisation, disinfection and antibiotic source collection.

nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Ischioanal fossa, pudendal canal and anal region
nodes.description: The ischioanal fossa contains fat that permits expansion of the anal canal.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Development of kidneys, bladder and urethra
nodes.description: Permanent kidney development requires reciprocal interaction between ureteric bud and metanephric mesenchyme.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Gonadal differentiation and genital ducts
nodes.description: Sertoli-cell anti-Mullerian hormone promotes paramesonephric regression, while Leydig-cell testosterone supports mesonephric duct differentiation.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: External genital development and gonadal descent
nodes.description: The processus vaginalis is a peritoneal extension that precedes testicular descent.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Neck triangles and surface orientation
nodes.description: Surface triangles organize access to deeper structures; they are not walled compartments.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Cervical fascia, carotid sheath and sympathetic trunk
nodes.description: The vagus lies posteriorly between the main vascular elements of the sheath; the sympathetic trunk lies posterior to the sheath rather than inside it.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Head and neck arteries, veins and lymphatics
nodes.description: The internal carotid supplies intracranial and orbital territories after ascending through the neck without typical cervical branches.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Oral cavity, palate and teeth
nodes.description: The vestibule lies between lips or cheeks and teeth, whereas the oral cavity proper lies inside the dental arches.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Salivary glands and their nerve routes
nodes.description: Passing through a gland does not mean innervating its secretion.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Mastication, TMJ and deep facial spaces
nodes.description: The TMJ disc divides the joint into compartments supporting rotation and translation.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Nasal cavity and paranasal drainage
nodes.description: A meatus lies below its corresponding concha.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Pharynx, tonsils and swallowing
nodes.description: Swallowing coordinates several barriers and propulsive actions.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Laryngeal skeleton, muscles and innervation
nodes.description: Abduction opens the rima glottidis; adduction brings the folds together.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Skull foramina, scalp and facial layers
nodes.description: A skull opening is a route, not a nerve's destination.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Orbit, eyeball and visual pathway
nodes.description: The orbit has a superior roof, medial wall, floor and lateral wall surrounding the globe and extraocular muscles.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: External, middle and inner ear
nodes.description: The external acoustic meatus conducts sound to the tympanic membrane.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Cranial nerve nuclei and functional columns
nodes.description: Opening of the fourth-ventricle region spreads the dorsal sensory plates laterally, leaving motor columns more medial.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Ocular motor nerves and lesion localization
nodes.description: Lateral rectus abducts the eye, so an isolated VI lesion weakens outward movement.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Trigeminal divisions and sensory territories
nodes.description: V1 and V2 are sensory divisions; V3 carries both sensory and branchial motor fibers.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Facial nerve course and branch functions
nodes.description: The facial nerve gives off branches at different points in its course.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Glossopharyngeal, vagus, accessory and hypoglossal nerves
nodes.description: IX, X and XI share the jugular foramen, while XII has a separate exit.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Cranial parasympathetic ganglia
nodes.description: Autonomic and sensory ganglia have different jobs.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Meninges, dural folds and intracranial spaces
nodes.description: Dura forms folds supporting and separating brain regions.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Dural venous sinuses and cavernous sinus relations
nodes.description: The cavernous sinus is lateral to the sella.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Cerebral arteries, territories and collateral routes
nodes.description: ACA mainly serves medial frontal and parietal surfaces, MCA much of the lateral hemisphere, and PCA occipital and inferior temporal territories.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Ventricles, CSF flow and internal landmarks
nodes.description: CSF flows from lateral ventricles through interventricular foramina to the third ventricle, then through the aqueduct to the fourth.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Basal ganglia, internal capsule and diencephalon
nodes.description: The internal capsule is white matter between deep gray-matter structures.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Brainstem landmarks and crossed findings
nodes.description: Localization combines level, side and pathway.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Cerebellum, peduncles and fourth ventricle
nodes.description: The middle peduncle carries extensive input from pontine nuclei, the inferior peduncle carries multiple spinal, vestibular and medullary connections, and the superior peduncle is predominantly an output route.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Spinal cord, meninges and long pathways
nodes.description: Dorsal columns carry discriminative touch, vibration and conscious proprioception ipsilaterally to the medulla before crossing.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Pharyngeal arches, pouches and arch arteries
nodes.description: Pouches are endodermal, grooves are ectodermal and arches contain mesenchymal tissue with characteristic vessels and nerves.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Development of face, palate and special senses
nodes.description: Inductive interactions connect tissues with different origins.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Brain vesicles, neural tube and spinal development
nodes.description: The lumen is preserved as surrounding neural tissue expands.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Bone structure and connections between bones
nodes.description: Bone shape predicts broad mechanical roles, but size alone does not define the category: phalanges are long bones despite being small.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Synovial joint design and movement
nodes.description: Articular cartilage reduces friction and distributes load, while the fibrous capsule encloses the joint and synovium contributes to the fluid environment.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Muscle architecture, actions and innervation
nodes.description: A muscle produces torque according to force and moment arm.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Vertebral column and regional vertebrae
nodes.description: Typical cervical vertebrae have transverse foramina, thoracic vertebrae articulate with ribs, and lumbar vertebrae have large weight-bearing bodies.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Atlas, axis and craniovertebral movement
nodes.description: The atlas forms a ring around the dens and articulates with occipital condyles above.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Intervertebral discs and spinal ligaments
nodes.description: The annulus resists tensile stresses around a hydrated nucleus, distributing compressive loads.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Back muscle layers and segmental innervation
nodes.description: Intrinsic back muscles retain segmental posterior-ramus supply and act on the vertebral column.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Clavicle, scapula and shoulder girdle joints
nodes.description: The clavicle acts as a strut supporting the scapula away from the thorax.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Glenohumeral joint and rotator cuff
nodes.description: The cuff consists of supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor and subscapularis.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Axilla, axillary artery and scapular spaces
nodes.description: The axillary nerve travels with posterior circumflex humeral vessels around the surgical neck.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Arm compartments and elbow relationships
nodes.description: Anterior arm muscles mainly flex the elbow and receive musculocutaneous supply; posterior muscles extend through radial supply.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Cubital fossa and forearm compartments
nodes.description: Most anterior forearm muscles receive median supply, but flexor carpi ulnaris and the medial part of flexor digitorum profundus are ulnar exceptions.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Wrist, carpal tunnel and anatomical snuffbox
nodes.description: The tunnel contains the median nerve and nine long flexor tendons: four superficial finger flexors, four deep finger flexors and one long thumb flexor.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Intrinsic hand muscles and functional nerve tests
nodes.description: Interossei control finger abduction and adduction relative to the middle-finger axis and contribute to MCP flexion with IP extension through extensor expansions.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Upper limb vessels and lymphatic routes
nodes.description: The arterial route changes names at landmarks: subclavian becomes axillary at the lateral first rib, then brachial at the inferior border of teres major.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Pelvic girdle and hip bone landmarks
nodes.description: Ilium, ischium and pubis meet around the acetabulum.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Hip joint stability and femoral head supply
nodes.description: The deep acetabulum and labrum provide bony and fibrocartilaginous stability, while capsular ligaments tighten in extension.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Gluteal region and the piriformis landmark
nodes.description: The stance-side gluteus medius and minimus generate an abduction moment that keeps the opposite pelvis from dropping.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Thigh compartments and muscle actions
nodes.description: Compartment rules connect action and innervation: anterior thigh largely uses femoral supply, medial thigh obturator, and posterior thigh sciatic divisions.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Femoral triangle, sheath and adductor canal
nodes.description: The lateral-to-medial order under the inguinal ligament is nerve, artery, vein and femoral canal.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Knee ligaments, menisci and movement
nodes.description: ACL and PCL names describe their tibial attachments, and their actions should specify which bone moves relative to which.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Popliteal fossa and neurovascular depth
nodes.description: The artery lies deepest against the fossa floor, while the tibial nerve is most superficial in the central bundle.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Leg compartments and ankle actions
nodes.description: Anterior muscles chiefly dorsiflex the ankle and extend toes; lateral muscles chiefly evert through superficial fibular supply.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Ankle, tarsal tunnel and foot arches
nodes.description: The talocrural mortise mainly permits dorsiflexion and plantarflexion.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Plantar muscles and nerve territories
nodes.description: The medial plantar nerve supplies a smaller muscle group including abductor hallucis, flexor digitorum brevis, flexor hallucis brevis and the first lumbrical.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Lower limb arteries, veins and lymphatics
nodes.description: Femoral artery becomes popliteal after the adductor hiatus, then supplies tibial routes toward the foot.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Lumbar and sacral plexuses across the limb
nodes.description: The femoral nerve arises from lumbar plexus roots L2-L4 and supplies knee extensors before its saphenous sensory continuation.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Neck muscles and hyoid relationships
nodes.description: A nerve can carry hitchhiking fibers from another source.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Regional lymph drainage and crossing territories
nodes.description: Lymphatic maps depend on tissue identity and development, not just present-day surface location.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Early patterning and limb development
nodes.description: Limb patterning has several axes.
nodes.subject: anatomy

nodes.title: Vertebral and skull development
nodes.description: Sclerotome cells surround the notochord and neural tube, then resegment so adjacent halves contribute to each vertebra.
nodes.subject: anatomy
